title: == vs ===
definition: Double equals `==` (Loose Equality) compares two values after attempting to implicitly coerce them to the same type. Triple equals `===` (Strict Equality) compares both value AND type without doing any conversion.
simpleExplanation: Loose equality `==` is like a bartender who accepts a hand-drawn picture of an ID as proof of age. Strict equality `===` checks both the ID and scans it to make sure it's legally valid.
realWorldExample: Always using `===` in React and modern JavaScript to prevent bizarre bugs where `0 == false` returns `true`.

basic: Why should you almost always use `===` instead of `==`?
intermediate: Is there ever a good reason to use `==`?
advanced: What is `Object.is()` and how does it differ from `===`?

answers.question: Is there ever a good reason to use ==?
answers.answer: Rarely, but checking `if (val == null)` is a shorthand way to check if a value is EITHER `null` OR `undefined` simultaneously, because `null == undefined` is true.

answers.question: What is Object.is()?
answers.answer: `Object.is()` is exactly like `===` except for two edge cases: it considers `NaN === NaN` to be true (unlike strict equality), and distinguishes between `-0` and `+0`.
